To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
commercialist scientists’ boundary work with postdoctoral scientists has implications for postdoctoral training.
commercialist scientists’ strategies for maintaining the boundaries between the fields of commercial science and traditional science have implications for postdoctoral socialization.

1) commercialist scientists’ boundary work between science and the commercial world is characterized by the use of three rules that demarcate science from the market: (1) “science first”; (2) “science is a public good”; and (3) “science is not a commodity”; and 2) commercialist scientists used postdoctoral trainees to segment the commercial from the scientific, thus creating a boundary between the fields of the market and science.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which the boundary work of academic scientists has consequences for the professional socialization of trainees.
the boundary work of commercialists in academe and the implications of this work for the professional socialization of postdoctoral researchers.
how the boundary work of commercialist scientists affects postdoctoral training and the professionalization process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
commercialists’ boundary work is a form of professional socialization in which postdoctoral scientists are used as boundary objects.
the boundary work of commercialist scientists in academe has implications for the professional socialization of postdoctoral researchers.
the boundary work of commercially oriented scientists has implications for the socialization of postdoctoral and graduate students into the academic professions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the liminality of postdocs and the rules they are asked to follow by commercialists are not conducive to their professional development.
commercialist scientists’ boundary work has important implications for postdoctoral scientists’ professional socialization and the health of the professoriate.
the commercialist scientists’ boundary work, which relies on postdocs, is not only a threat to the traditional norms of science, but also to the long term viability of the scientific profession.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the commercialization of science is not simply a matter of the commodification of science.
postdocs are a critical part of the boundary between science and the commercial world and that the boundary is not as clear as it might appear.
commercialist strategies for demarcation are a product of their field positions and the rules that operate within fields.
